statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r, the following holds: len(r) = m, every row r[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m, and for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] = |L(i,j) - R(i,j)|, where L(i,j) is the number of distinct integer values among the set { grid[x][y] | 0 <= x < i, 0 <= y < j, x - y = i - j }, and R(i,j) is the number of distinct integer values among the set { grid[x][y] | i < x < m, j < y < n, x - y = i - j }. Here |z| denotes the absolute value of the integer z.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: For every grid satisfying the preconditions, difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r (it does not fail).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid (len(r) = m and len(r[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m), then for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 0 <= r[i][j].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid, for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] <= max(min(i,j), min(m - 1 - i, n - 1 - j)).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid, if m = 1 or n = 1, then for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid, if m = 2 and n = 2, then r[0][0] = 1, r[0][1] = 0, r[1][0] = 0, and r[1][1] = 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r and difference_of_distinct_values rot returns a result r', and both r and r' have the same dimensions as their inputs (len(r) = m, len(r[i]) = n, len(r') = m, len(r'[x]) = n), then for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] = r'[m - 1 - i][n - 1 - j].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50. Let rot be the m x n grid defined by rot[x][y] = grid[m - 1 - x][n - 1 - y] for 0 <= x < m and 0 <= y < n.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values g returns r and difference_of_distinct_values g' returns r', and both r and r' have the same dimensions as their inputs, then for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, if for every x,y with 0 <= x < m and 0 <= y < n and x - y = i - j we have g[x][y] = g'[x][y], then r[i][j] = r'[i][j].
preconditions: Let g and g' be two grids satisfying the problem constraints with the same dimensions: let m = len(g) = len(g'), n = len(g[0]) = len(g'[0]), with 1 <= m <= 50 and 1 <= n <= 50; every row of g and of g' has length n, and all entries of both grids are between 1 and 50 inclusive.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values g returns r and difference_of_distinct_values g' returns r', and both r and r' have the same dimensions as their inputs, then r[p][q] = r'[p][q].
preconditions: Let g be a grid satisfying the problem constraints with m = len(g), n = len(g[0]), 1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= n <= 50, every row length n, and all entries between 1 and 50 inclusive. Let p,q satisfy 0 <= p < m and 0 <= q < n. Let g' be another grid satisfying the same constraints with the same m,n and with g'[i][j] = g[i][j] for every (i,j) except possibly (i,j) = (p,q).

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values g returns r and difference_of_distinct_values g' returns r', and both r and r' have the same dimensions as their inputs, then for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] = r'[i][j].
preconditions: Let g be a grid satisfying the problem constraints with m = len(g), n = len(g[0]), 1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= n <= 50, every row length n, and all entries between 1 and 50 inclusive. Let t be an integer such that 1 <= g[i][j] + t <= 50 for every i,j. Let g' be the grid defined by g'[i][j] = g[i][j] + t for every i,j.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid, for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, if for all x,y with 0 <= x < m and 0 <= y < n and x - y = i - j we have grid[x][y] = grid[i][j], then r[i][j] = |A(i,j) - B(i,j)|, where A(i,j) = 1 if there exist x,y with 0 <= x < i, 0 <= y < j, and x - y = i - j, and A(i,j) = 0 otherwise; and B(i,j) = 1 if there exist x,y with i < x < m, j < y < n, and x - y = i - j, and B(i,j) = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid, r[0][n - 1] = 0 and r[m - 1][0] = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns r and difference_of_distinct_values gridT returns rT, and both have the same dimensions as their inputs (len(r) = m, len(r[i]) = n, len(rT) = n, len(rT[x]) = m), then for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] = rT[j][i].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50. Let gridT be the n x m grid defined by gridT[x][y] = grid[y][x] for 0 <= x < n and 0 <= y < m.

statement: Whenever difference_of_distinct_values grid returns a result r of the same dimensions as grid, for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, if the values on the diagonal x - y = i - j are pairwise distinct (that is, for all (x,y) and (u,v) with 0 <= x,u < m, 0 <= y,v < n, x - y = i - j, u - v = i - j, and (x,y) != (u,v), we have grid[x][y] != grid[u][v]), then r[i][j] = |min(i,j) - min(m - 1 - i, n - 1 - j)|.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume 1 <= m <= 50. Let n = len(grid[0]); assume 1 <= n <= 50. Assume every row grid[i] has length n for 0 <= i < m. Assume for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 50.
